submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 2 cm thickness is the optimal choice, delivering 3.814 sigma pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c - the highest performance among all valid configurations. This exceeds the minimum requirement of 3.5 sigma by a comfortable margin of 0.314 sigma. Critically, R1 is the only radiator candidate that passes the transparency constraint, with less than 10% transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing testing. Radiators R2 and R3 both fail this hard requirement and cannot be considered. Among the three valid R1 thickness options (2, 3, and 4 cm), the 2 cm configuration provides superior separation performance while using less material, making it the clear optimal choice for maximizing hadron identification capability over the detector's operational lifetime.
